l4_steps.name: Define ground handling scope and service requirements
l4_steps.input: Network expansion plan, station opening schedule, incumbent contract expiry notice
l4_steps.output: Ground handling scope document covering ramp, fuelling, deicing, ULD, and cleaning
l4_steps.kpi: Scope document published within 10 business days of trigger event
l4_steps.pain_point: Scope creep when station-specific deicing or narrow-body-only ramp constraints are not captured early, leading to SLA gaps on first winter ops

l4_steps.name: Issue RFP to pre-qualified ground handlers
l4_steps.input: Approved scope document, approved vendor panel list from supplier master
l4_steps.output: Published RFP with evaluation scorecard, response deadline, and mandatory IATA SGHA annex B template
l4_steps.kpi: RFP issued within 5 business days of scope sign-off; minimum 3 qualified bidders invited
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin vendor panels at secondary airports (e.g. single-handler markets) reduce competitive tension and inflate unit rates by up to 25% vs hub markets

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor proposals against qualification criteria
l4_steps.input: Vendor RFP responses, IATA ISAGO audit certificates, IOSA-compliant safety declarations
l4_steps.output: Scored evaluation matrix; shortlist of 1–2 vendors approved for site audit
l4_steps.kpi: Evaluation completed within 15 business days of RFP close; minimum ISAGO score ≥ 80%
l4_steps.pain_point: ISAGO certificates from some regional handlers are expired or cover a different station than the one being contracted, requiring manual verification against IATA ISAGO registry

l4_steps.name: Conduct on-site capability and safety audit
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendor details, ISAGO report, audit checklist aligned to IATA AHM 810
l4_steps.output: Audit report with pass/fail rating per category; safety risk register entry in Archer GRC
l4_steps.kpi: On-site audit completed within 20 business days of shortlist; zero critical findings to proceed
l4_steps.pain_point: Handlers at code-share or alliance partner hubs may operate under local airport authority waivers that do not meet airline-specific safety standards, creating liability exposure

l4_steps.name: Negotiate SLA terms, turnaround targets, and penalty rates
l4_steps.input: Audit-cleared vendor, benchmark turnaround data from SITA Airport Management System, peer airline SLA benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Agreed SLA schedule: D0 target ≥78%, bag delivery ≤20 min, FOD check compliance 100%
l4_steps.kpi: SLA negotiation concluded within 10 business days; penalty trigger at ≥3 consecutive monthly SLA breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Handlers resist penalty clauses tied to D0 when ATC or fuel delays (outside handler control) are not explicitly excluded in the SLA attribution model

l4_steps.name: Conduct legal and aviation safety compliance review
l4_steps.input: Draft IATA SGHA Main Agreement and Annex B, insurance certificates, local aviation authority operating permit
l4_steps.output: Legal sign-off memo; contract approved or returned with redlines
l4_steps.kpi: Legal review cycle ≤ 15 business days; zero unresolved liability caps at execution
l4_steps.pain_point: Jurisdictional variation in ground handling regulations (e.g. EU Groundhandling Directive 96/67/EC vs. FAA Part 139 requirements for US stations) extends review cycles for multi-station contracts

l4_steps.name: Execute contract and issue purchase order
l4_steps.input: Countersigned SGHA, approved budget in SAP cost centre, contract start date confirmed with station team
l4_steps.output: Executed contract stored in SAP Ariba repository; PO issued in SAP S/4HANA; vendor activated in supplier master
l4_steps.kpi: PO issued within 2 business days of contract execution; contract visible in SAP Ariba within same day
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data re-entry when contracts are executed outside SAP Ariba (e.g. via email exchange) causes vendor master mismatches and delayed invoice matching

l4_steps.name: Register vendor in airport operations system
l4_steps.input: Executed contract, vendor contact list, station codes, service scope per aircraft type
l4_steps.output: Vendor profile active in SITA AMS with service assignments per stand and aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor profile configured and tested in SITA AMS ≥ 5 business days before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS vendor profiles are station-scoped; multi-station contracts require separate profile creation at each station, increasing setup time and risk of configuration inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Configure KPI monitoring thresholds in performance dashboard
l4_steps.input: Contracted SLA targets, SITA AMS data feeds, Amadeus Airport Management turnaround data
l4_steps.output: Live Tableau dashboard with amber/red KPI alerts per vendor, per station, per service type
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard live and validated against 5 historical flights before go-live; alert latency ≤ 1 hour from event
l4_steps.pain_point: Data latency between Amadeus Airport Management and Tableau can exceed 90 minutes during peak schedules, causing delayed breach detection and missed real-time intervention windows

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-operations readiness assessment
l4_steps.input: Vendor staff roster, GSE serviceability checklist, SITA AMS profile test results, safety induction completion records
l4_steps.output: Signed go/no-go readiness certificate; open items logged in Archer GRC if any
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of vendor staff complete airline safety induction before go-live; GSE serviceability ≥ 95% on day 1
l4_steps.pain_point: High staff turnover at ground handling contractors (industry average >40% p.a.) means safety induction records in SAP SuccessFactors are frequently out of date within weeks of go-live

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily turnaround performance data from ops systems
l4_steps.input: SITA AMS event logs (chocks-on, door-open, door-close, chocks-off), ACARS timestamps, fuelling records
l4_steps.output: Validated daily performance dataset per vendor per flight sector
l4_steps.kpi: ≥ 98% of flights matched to vendor records within 24 hours; data completeness ≥ 99%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS timestamp gaps on narrow-body short-haul sectors (sub-45-min turns) create ambiguous attribution when two ground handlers operate at adjacent stands simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly vendor performance scorecard
l4_steps.input: 30-day aggregated performance dataset, contracted SLA thresholds, prior month scorecard for trend analysis
l4_steps.output: Vendor scorecard PDF: D0 %, bag delivery time, FOD incidents, safety events, delay attribution
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard issued by business day 5 of following month; D0 target ≥78%, bag delivery ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay attribution disputes between airline and vendor are common where root-cause coding (e.g. IATA delay code 93 vs. 61) is entered by different parties, inflating apparent handler performance

l4_steps.name: Assess KPI compliance against contracted SLA thresholds
l4_steps.input: Monthly vendor scorecard, SLA penalty schedule from SAP Ariba contract record
l4_steps.output: Compliance verdict per KPI: Green (met), Amber (within cure period), Red (penalty triggered)
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance assessment completed within 2 business days of scorecard publication; penalty invoice raised within 5 days of Red verdict
l4_steps.pain_point: SLA cure periods (typically 30 days) allow repeated near-misses that never formally trigger penalties, masking systemic under-performance until a major disruption event

l4_steps.name: Issue formal performance improvement notice to vendor
l4_steps.input: Red KPI verdict, scorecard evidence, prior month trend data, contract penalty clause reference
l4_steps.output: Formal written performance improvement plan (PIP) with 30/60/90-day milestones logged in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: PIP issued within 5 business days of Red verdict; vendor root-cause response required within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground handlers often attribute performance failures to airline-side delays (late aircraft, late pax boarding) that are poorly documented, making PIP enforcement difficult without granular ACARS evidence

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual vendor safety and compliance audit
l4_steps.input: 12-month performance data, open PIP items, ISAGO renewal status, local regulatory inspection reports
l4_steps.output: Annual audit report with risk rating (Low/Medium/High) and mandatory corrective action items
l4_steps.kpi: Annual audit completed ≥ 90 days before contract renewal date; zero High-risk open findings at renewal
l4_steps.pain_point: ISAGO audit cycles (every 2 years) do not align with annual contract reviews, creating a 12-month window where compliance status is unverified between ISAGO renewal and airline audit

l4_steps.name: Evaluate contract renewal versus re-tender decision
l4_steps.input: Annual audit report, 12-month KPI scorecard trend, market rate benchmarks, strategic station growth plan
l4_steps.output: Renewal or re-tender recommendation memo approved by VP Ground Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Decision memo issued ≥ 60 days before contract expiry; re-tender initiated if 12-month D0 average < 75%
l4_steps.pain_point: At captive single-handler airports, re-tender is not a credible threat, weakening commercial leverage and often resulting in rate increases at renewal regardless of performance history

l4_steps.name: Execute contract renewal or initiate new sourcing cycle
l4_steps.input: Approved renewal or re-tender decision memo, updated scope (if changed), revised SLA targets
l4_steps.output: Renewed contract executed in SAP Ariba OR new RFP issued back at step 1.2; vendor master updated
l4_steps.kpi: Contract renewal executed ≥ 30 days before expiry; zero lapse in contractual coverage at any station
l4_steps.pain_point: Contract lapses during re-tender transitions force reliance on month-to-month SGHA extensions at full tariff rates, increasing ground handling costs by 15–30% until new contract is executed
